13	// ServiceStats tracks transfer statistics for a single service.
14	type ServiceStats struct {
15		Name          string `json:"name"`
16		Requests      int    `json:"requests"`
17		RequestBytes  int64  `json:"requestBytes"`
18		ResponseBytes int64  `json:"responseBytes"`
19		Wants         int    `json:"wants"`
20		Haves         int    `json:"haves"`
21		Commands      int    `json:"commands"`
22	}
23	
24	// Stats holds the collected transfer statistics.
25	type Stats struct {
26		Enabled bool                     `json:"enabled"`
27		Items   map[string]*ServiceStats `json:"items"`
28	}
29	
30	// statsCollector is a concurrency-safe stats collector (issue #8).
31	type statsCollector struct {
32		enabled bool
33		mu      sync.Mutex
34		items   map[string]*ServiceStats
35	}
36	
37	func newStats(enabled bool) *statsCollector {
38		return &statsCollector{enabled: enabled, items: map[string]*ServiceStats{}}
39	}
40	
41	func (s *statsCollector) ensure(name string) *ServiceStats {
42		item, ok := s.items[name]
43		if !ok {
44			item = &ServiceStats{Name: name}
45			s.items[name] = item
46		}
47		return item
48	}
49	
50	func (s *statsCollector) recordRoundTrip(name string, requestBytes, responseBytes int64) {
51		if !s.enabled {
52			return
53		}
54		s.mu.Lock()
55		defer s.mu.Unlock()
56		item := s.ensure(name)
57		item.Requests++
58		item.RequestBytes += requestBytes
59		item.ResponseBytes += responseBytes
60	}
61	
62	func (s *statsCollector) snapshot() Stats {
63		s.mu.Lock()
64		defer s.mu.Unlock()
65		out := Stats{Enabled: s.enabled, Items: make(map[string]*ServiceStats, len(s.items))}
66		for key, item := range s.items {
67			copyItem := *item
68			out.Items[key] = &copyItem
69		}
70		return out
71	}
72	
73	// countingRoundTripper wraps an HTTP transport to record transfer stats.
74	type countingRoundTripper struct {
75		base  http.RoundTripper
76		label string
77		stats *statsCollector
78	}
79	
80	func (rt *countingRoundTripper) RoundTrip(req *http.Request) (*http.Response, error) {
81		res, err := rt.base.RoundTrip(req)
82		if err != nil {
83			return nil, fmt.Errorf("round trip: %w", err)
84		}
85	
86		serviceName := req.Header.Get(gitproto.StatsPhaseHeader)
87		if serviceName == "" {
88			serviceName = req.URL.Query().Get("service")
89			if serviceName == "" {
90				serviceName = strings.TrimPrefix(req.URL.Path[strings.LastIndex(req.URL.Path, "/")+1:], "/")
91			}
92		}
93		name := strings.TrimSpace(rt.label + " " + serviceName)
94		requestBytes := req.ContentLength
95		if requestBytes < 0 {
96			requestBytes = 0
97		}
98	
99		res.Body = &countingReadCloser{
100			ReadCloser: res.Body,
101			onClose: func(n int64) {
102				rt.stats.recordRoundTrip(name, requestBytes, n)
103			},
104		}
105		return res, nil
106	}
107	
108	type countingReadCloser struct {
109		io.ReadCloser
110	
111		n       int64
112		onClose func(int64)
113	}
114	
115	func (c *countingReadCloser) Read(p []byte) (int, error) {
116		n, err := c.ReadCloser.Read(p)
117		c.n += int64(n)
118		return n, err //nolint:wrapcheck // Read must preserve io.EOF for io.Reader contract
119	}
120	
121	func (c *countingReadCloser) Close() error {
122		err := c.ReadCloser.Close()
123		if c.onClose != nil {
124			c.onClose(c.n)
125			c.onClose = nil
126		}
127		if err != nil {
128			return fmt.Errorf("close: %w", err)
129		}
130		return nil
131	}

14	func newFetchCmd() *cobra.Command {

16			haveRefs      []string
17			haveHashesRaw []string
18			jsonOutput    bool

23		)
24	
25		cmd := &cobra.Command{
26			Use:           "fetch [flags] <source-url>",
27			Short:         "Negotiate a fetch against the source and report packed objects",
28			Args:          cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),
29			SilenceErrors: true,
30			SilenceUsage:  true,
31			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
32				req.Protocol = gitsync.ProtocolMode(protocolVal)
33	
34				if req.Source.URL == "" && len(args) > 0 {
35					req.Source.URL = args[0]
36				}
37				if req.Source.URL == "" {
38					return errors.New("fetch requires a source repository URL")
39				}
40				if branches != "" {
41					req.Scope.Branches = splitCSV(branches)
42				}
43	
44				haveHashes := make([]plumbing.Hash, 0, len(haveHashesRaw))
45				for _, raw := range haveHashesRaw {
46					hash := plumbing.NewHash(strings.TrimSpace(raw))
47					if hash.IsZero() {
48						return fmt.Errorf("invalid --have %q", raw)
49					}
50					haveHashes = append(haveHashes, hash)
51				}
52	
53				req.HaveRefs = append(req.HaveRefs, haveRefs...)
54				req.HaveHashes = append(req.HaveHashes, haveHashes...)
55	
56				result, err := unstable.New(unstable.Options{
57					Auth: gitsync.StaticAuthProvider{Source: sourceAuth},
58				}).Fetch(cmd.Context(), req)
59				if err != nil {
60					return fmt.Errorf("fetch: %w", err)
61				}
62				printOutput(jsonOutput, result)
63				return nil
64			},
65		}
66	
67		addSourceEndpoint(cmd, &req.Source)

373	// --- Session setup (issue #12) ---
374	
375	// syncSession holds the shared state for a sync operation, reducing
376	// setup duplication across Run, Bootstrap, Probe, and Fetch.
377	type syncSession struct {
378		cfg             Config
379		stats           *statsCollector
380		logger          *slog.Logger
381		sourceConn      *gitproto.Conn
382		sourceService   *gitproto.RefService
383		sourceRefMap    map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash
384		target          *targetSession
385		measurementDone func() Measurement
386	}
387	
388	type targetSession struct {
389		conn     *gitproto.Conn
390		adv      *packp.AdvRefs
391		refMap   map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash
392		features gitproto.TargetFeatures
393		policy   planner.RelayTargetPolicy
394		pusher   gitproto.Pusher
395	}
396	
397	// newSession performs the shared setup: protocol validation, mapping validation,
398	// connection creation, and ref discovery.
399	func newSession(ctx context.Context, cfg Config, needTarget bool) (*syncSession, error) {
400		mode, err := validation.NormalizeProtocolMode(cfg.ProtocolMode)
401		if err != nil {
402			return nil, fmt.Errorf("normalize protocol mode: %w", err)
403		}
404		cfg.ProtocolMode = mode
405		switch cfg.Mode {
406		case "", modeSync:
407			cfg.Mode = modeSync
408		case modeReplicate:
409		default:
410			return nil, fmt.Errorf("unsupported operation mode %q", cfg.Mode)
411		}
412		if _, err := validation.ValidateMappings(cfg.Mappings); err != nil {
413			return nil, fmt.Errorf("validate mappings: %w", err)
414		}
415		if cfg.Mode == modeReplicate && cfg.Force {
416			return nil, errors.New("replicate does not support --force; use sync instead")
417		}
418		if needTarget {
419			if err := validation.ValidateEndpoints(cfg.Source.URL, cfg.Target.URL); err != nil {
420				return nil, fmt.Errorf("validate endpoints: %w", err)
421			}
422		}
423	
424		s := &syncSession{
425			cfg:             cfg,
426			stats:           newStats(cfg.ShowStats),
427			measurementDone: startMeasurement(cfg.MeasureMemory),
428		}
429		if cfg.Verbose {
430			s.logger = slog.New(slog.NewTextHandler(os.Stderr, &slog.HandlerOptions{
431				Level: slog.LevelInfo,
432			}))
433		}
434	
435		s.sourceConn, err = newConn(cfg.Source, "source", s.stats, cfg.HTTPClient)
436		if err != nil {
437			return nil, fmt.Errorf("create source transport: %w", err)
438		}
439	
440		refPrefixes := planner.RefPrefixes(cfg.Mappings, cfg.IncludeTags)
441		sourceRefs, sourceService, err := gitproto.ListSourceRefs(ctx, s.sourceConn, cfg.ProtocolMode, refPrefixes)
442		if err != nil {
443			return nil, fmt.Errorf("list source refs: %w", err)
444		}
445		sourceService.Verbose = cfg.Verbose
446		s.sourceService = sourceService
447		s.sourceRefMap = gitproto.RefHashMap(sourceRefs)
448	
449		if needTarget {
450			targetConn, err := newConn(cfg.Target, "target", s.stats, cfg.HTTPClient)
451			if err != nil {
452				return nil, fmt.Errorf("create target transport: %w", err)
453			}
454			targetAdv, err := gitproto.AdvertisedRefsV1(ctx, targetConn, transport.ReceivePackService)
455			if err != nil {
456				return nil, fmt.Errorf("list target refs: %w", err)
457			}
458			targetRefSlice, err := gitproto.AdvRefsToSlice(targetAdv)
459			if err != nil {
460				return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode target refs: %w", err)
461			}
462			targetRefMap := gitproto.RefHashMap(targetRefSlice)
463			targetFeatures := gitproto.TargetFeaturesFromAdvRefs(targetAdv)
464			s.target = &targetSession{
465				conn:     targetConn,
466				adv:      targetAdv,
467				refMap:   targetRefMap,
468				features: targetFeatures,
469				policy: planner.RelayTargetPolicy{
470					CapabilitiesKnown: targetFeatures.Known,
471					NoThin:            targetFeatures.NoThin,
472				},
473				pusher: gitproto.NewPusher(targetConn, targetAdv, cfg.Verbose),
474			}
475		}
476	
477		return s, nil
478	}

483	func Run(ctx context.Context, cfg Config) (Result, error) {
484		s, err := newSession(ctx, cfg, true)
485		if err != nil {
486			return Result{}, err
487		}
488		if s.cfg.Mode == modeReplicate {
489			return s.runReplicate(ctx)

1	package syncer
2	
3	import (
4		"runtime"
5		"sync"
6		"time"
7	)
8	
9	// Measurement holds performance measurement data.
10	type Measurement struct {
11		Enabled            bool   `json:"enabled"`
12		ElapsedMillis      int64  `json:"elapsedMillis"`
13		PeakAllocBytes     uint64 `json:"peakAllocBytes"`
14		PeakHeapInuseBytes uint64 `json:"peakHeapInuseBytes"`
15		TotalAllocBytes    uint64 `json:"totalAllocBytes"`
16		GCCount            uint32 `json:"gcCount"`
17	}
18	
19	func startMeasurement(enabled bool) func() Measurement {
20		if !enabled {
21			return func() Measurement { return Measurement{} }
22		}
23	
24		start := time.Now()
25		var startStats runtime.MemStats
26		runtime.ReadMemStats(&startStats)
27	
28		done := make(chan struct{})
29		var (
30			mu            sync.Mutex
31			peakAlloc     = startStats.Alloc
32			peakHeapInuse = startStats.HeapInuse
33			result        Measurement
34		)
35	
36		go func() {
37			ticker := time.NewTicker(200 * time.Millisecond)
38			defer ticker.Stop()
39			for {
40				select {
41				case <-done:
42					return
43				case <-ticker.C:
44					var current runtime.MemStats
45					runtime.ReadMemStats(&current)
46					mu.Lock()
47					if current.Alloc > peakAlloc {
48						peakAlloc = current.Alloc
49					}
50					if current.HeapInuse > peakHeapInuse {
51						peakHeapInuse = current.HeapInuse
52					}
53					mu.Unlock()
54				}
55			}
56		}()
57	
58		var once sync.Once
59		return func() Measurement {
60			once.Do(func() {
61				close(done)
62				var endStats runtime.MemStats
63				runtime.ReadMemStats(&endStats)
64				mu.Lock()
65				if endStats.Alloc > peakAlloc {
66					peakAlloc = endStats.Alloc
67				}
68				if endStats.HeapInuse > peakHeapInuse {
69					peakHeapInuse = endStats.HeapInuse
70				}
71				result = Measurement{
72					Enabled:            true,
73					ElapsedMillis:      time.Since(start).Milliseconds(),
74					PeakAllocBytes:     peakAlloc,
75					PeakHeapInuseBytes: peakHeapInuse,
76					TotalAllocBytes:    endStats.TotalAlloc - startStats.TotalAlloc,
77					GCCount:            endStats.NumGC - startStats.NumGC,
78				}
79				mu.Unlock()
80			})
81			return result
82		}
83	}
84	
```

> AGENT

Not a huge effort — the plumbing is already in place. `countingReadCloser.Read` (internal/syncer/stats.go:115) already sees every byte flowing through both source and target HTTP bodies; right now we only surface the total on `Close`. The two flavors:

- **End-of-run throughput (tiny):** `--stats` already gives bytes per service and `--measure-memory` already gives elapsed ms. Adding a derived `bytes/elapsed` line to the human output is a few lines in the print path. ~30 min of work.
- **Live progress on stderr (small-medium):** add an atomic byte counter shared across the counting readers, plus a ticker goroutine that prints `\rfetch: 42.1 MB @ 5.3 MB/s` on stderr behind a `--progress` flag (auto-off when `--json` or non-TTY). ~50–100 LOC, mostly in `stats.go` + a small renderer + flag wiring in `cmd/git-sync`. The tradeoff: a true % bar is hard because git smart-HTTP responses are chunked with no Content-Length, so it'd be throughput + bytes-so-far, not a percentage.

I'd start with the end-of-run number since it's nearly free, and only add the live ticker if you actually want feedback during long bootstraps. Want me to do either?

> DEVELOPER

Yeah I want both, ideally also separated for source and target, like how fast did we get data from the source and how fast did target take it (might be bound to network but still)

So also when doing a live ticket can we show both?

140	func (r Result) Lines() []string {
141		lines := make([]string, 0, len(r.Plans)+8)
142		for _, plan := range r.Plans {
143			lines = append(lines, planner.FormatPlanLine(plan))
144		}
145		summary := fmt.Sprintf(

147			r.Pushed, r.Deleted, r.Skipped, r.Blocked, r.OperationMode, r.Protocol, r.Relay, r.RelayMode, r.RelayReason, r.Batching, r.BatchCount, r.PlannedBatchCount,
148		)
149		if r.DryRun {
150			summary += " dry-run=true"
151		}
152		lines = append(lines, summary)
153		lines = append(lines, statsLines(r.Stats)...)
154		lines = append(lines, measurementLine(r.Measurement)...)
155		if r.BootstrapSuggested {
156			lines = append(lines, "hint: target refs are absent; bootstrap can seed them without local object storage")
157		}
158		if r.Batching && len(r.TempRefs) > 0 {
159			lines = append(lines, "batching: temp-refs="+strings.Join(r.TempRefs, ","))

263	func statsLines(s Stats) []string {
264		if !s.Enabled {
265			return nil
266		}
267		keys := make([]string, 0, len(s.Items))
268		for k := range s.Items {
269			keys = append(keys, k)
270		}
271		sort.Strings(keys)
272		var lines []string
273		for _, k := range keys {
274			item := s.Items[k]
275			lines = append(lines, fmt.Sprintf(
276				"stats: %s requests=%d request-bytes=%d response-bytes=%d wants=%d haves=%d commands=%d",
277				item.Name, item.Requests, item.RequestBytes, item.ResponseBytes, item.Wants, item.Haves, item.Commands,
278			))
279		}
280		return lines
281	}

116	func FromProbeResult(result syncer.ProbeResult) ProbeResult {
117		out := ProbeResult{
118			SourceURL:     result.SourceURL,
119			TargetURL:     result.TargetURL,
120			RequestedMode: result.RequestedMode,
121			Protocol:      result.Protocol,
122			RefPrefixes:   append([]string(nil), result.RefPrefixes...),
123			Capabilities:  append([]string(nil), result.Capabilities...),
124			TargetCaps:    append([]string(nil), result.TargetCaps...),
125			Refs:          make([]RefInfo, 0, len(result.Refs)),
126			Stats:         FromStats(result.Stats),
127			Measurement:   FromMeasurement(result.Measurement),
128		}
129		for _, ref := range result.Refs {
130			out.Refs = append(out.Refs, RefInfo{Name: ref.Name, Hash: ref.Hash.String()})
131		}
132		return out
133	}
134	
135	func FromSyncResult(result syncer.Result) SyncResult {
136		out := SyncResult{
137			Refs: make([]RefResult, 0, len(result.Plans)),
138			Counts: SyncCounts{
139				Applied: result.Pushed,
140				Skipped: result.Skipped,
141				Blocked: result.Blocked,
142				Deleted: result.Deleted,
143			},
144			Execution: ExecutionSummary{
145				DryRun:             result.DryRun,
146				Protocol:           result.Protocol,
147				OperationMode:      result.OperationMode,
148				Relay:              result.Relay,
149				TransferMode:       result.RelayMode,
150				Reason:             result.RelayReason,
151				BootstrapSuggested: result.BootstrapSuggested,
152				Batch: BatchSummary{
153					Enabled: result.Batching,
154					Planned: result.PlannedBatchCount,
155					Done:    result.BatchCount,
156				},
157			},
158			Stats:       FromStats(result.Stats),
159			Measurement: FromMeasurement(result.Measurement),
160		}
161		for _, plan := range result.Plans {
162			out.Refs = append(out.Refs, RefResult{
163				Branch:     plan.Branch,
164				SourceRef:  plan.SourceRef.String(),
165				TargetRef:  plan.TargetRef.String(),
166				SourceHash: HashString(plan.SourceHash),
167				TargetHash: HashString(plan.TargetHash),
168				Kind:       RefKind(plan.Kind),
169				Action:     Action(plan.Action),
170				Reason:     plan.Reason,
171			})
172		}
173		return out
174	}
175	
176	func FromStats(stats syncer.Stats) Stats {
177		out := Stats{Enabled: stats.Enabled, Items: make(map[string]*ServiceStats, len(stats.Items))}
178		for key, item := range stats.Items {
179			copyItem := *item
180			out.Items[key] = &ServiceStats{
181				Name:          copyItem.Name,
182				Requests:      copyItem.Requests,
183				RequestBytes:  copyItem.RequestBytes,
184				ResponseBytes: copyItem.ResponseBytes,
185				Wants:         copyItem.Wants,
186				Haves:         copyItem.Haves,
187				Commands:      copyItem.Commands,
188			}
189		}
190		return out
191	}
192	
193	func FromMeasurement(m syncer.Measurement) Measurement {
194		return Measurement{
195			Enabled:            m.Enabled,
196			ElapsedMillis:      m.ElapsedMillis,
197			PeakAllocBytes:     m.PeakAllocBytes,
198			PeakHeapInuseBytes: m.PeakHeapInuseBytes,
199			TotalAllocBytes:    m.TotalAllocBytes,
200			GCCount:            m.GCCount,
201		}
202	}
203	
204	func HashString(hash plumbing.Hash) string {
205		if hash.IsZero() {
206			return ""
207		}
208		return hash.String()
209	}

295	func newConn(raw Endpoint, label string, stats *statsCollector, httpClient *http.Client) (*gitproto.Conn, error) {
296		ep, err := transport.ParseURL(raw.URL)
297		if err != nil {
298			return nil, fmt.Errorf("parse endpoint: %w", err)
299		}
300		authEp := auth.Endpoint{
301			Username:      raw.Username,
302			Token:         raw.Token,
303			BearerToken:   raw.BearerToken,
304			SkipTLSVerify: raw.SkipTLSVerify,
305		}
306		authMethod, err := auth.Resolve(authEp, ep)
307		if err != nil {
308			return nil, fmt.Errorf("resolve auth: %w", err)
309		}
310		client := instrumentHTTPClient(httpClient, raw.SkipTLSVerify, label, stats)
311		conn := gitproto.NewConnWithHTTPClient(ep, label, authMethod, client)
312		conn.FollowInfoRefsRedirect = raw.FollowInfoRefsRedirect
313		return conn, nil
314	}
315	
316	func instrumentHTTPClient(base *http.Client, skipTLS bool, label string, stats *statsCollector) *http.Client {
317		if base == nil {
318			base = &http.Client{Transport: gitproto.NewHTTPTransport(skipTLS)}
319		}
320		clone := *base
321		baseRT := clone.Transport
322		if baseRT == nil {
323			baseRT = gitproto.NewHTTPTransport(skipTLS)
324		}
325		clone.Transport = &countingRoundTripper{base: baseRT, label: label, stats: stats}
326		return &clone
327	}
328	
329	func planConfig(cfg Config) planner.PlanConfig {
330		return planner.PlanConfig{
331			Branches:    cfg.Branches,
332			Mappings:    cfg.Mappings,
333			IncludeTags: cfg.IncludeTags,
334			Force:       cfg.Force,
335			Prune:       cfg.Prune,
336		}
337	}
338	
339	// needsLocalSourceClosure reports whether the sync must populate the
340	// in-memory store with the full source closure before running. The fetch
341	// is required when:
342	//   - Force or prune is set: incremental relay is disabled, so the
343	//     materialized fallback will run and needs the closure.
344	//   - Any desired ref already exists on target at a different hash: a
345	//     branch fast-forward check will need ancestry data, or a tag retarget
346	//     will route to materialized.
347	//
348	// When all desired refs are either skips (target hash matches source) or
349	// creates (target hash is zero), incremental relay handles the push without
350	// the closure — the upfront fetch would just be wasted bandwidth, since
351	// relay does its own FetchPack on the source.
352	func needsLocalSourceClosure(
353		cfg Config,
354		desired map[plumbing.ReferenceName]planner.DesiredRef,
355		targetRefs map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash,
356	) bool {
357		if cfg.Force || cfg.Prune {
358			return true
359		}
360		for targetRef, want := range desired {
361			targetHash := targetRefs[targetRef]
362			if targetHash.IsZero() {
363				continue
364			}
365			if targetHash == want.SourceHash {
366				continue
367			}
368			return true
369		}
370		return false
371	}

> AGENT

Yes — both is doable on one stderr line. Here's the approach I'd take, want to confirm before I start:

**Per-side accounting:** "source" = bytes streamed through the source HTTP transport (dominated by upload-pack response — what we *got* from the source). "target" = bytes streamed through the target transport (dominated by receive-pack request body — what we *pushed* to the target). I'll wrap both `req.Body` and `resp.Body` in the existing `countingRoundTripper`, with atomic byte counters per label so a ticker can sample without locking.

**End-of-run lines (under `--stats`):** add `throughput: source=42.1 MB @ 5.3 MB/s | target=38.7 MB @ 4.9 MB/s` derived from per-side bytes ÷ wall-clock elapsed.

**Live ticker (`--progress`):** goroutine prints `\rsource: 12.3 MB @ 4.5 MB/s · target: 8.1 MB @ 3.2 MB/s` to stderr every 200ms; auto-suppressed when stderr isn't a TTY or when `--json` is on.

Sound right? If yes I'll implement it — should be ~250-300 LOC across `internal/syncer/stats.go`, a new `progress.go`, syncer wiring, and flag plumbing.

73		Source      gitsync.Endpoint
74		Scope       gitsync.RefScope
75		IncludeTags bool
76		Protocol    gitsync.ProtocolMode
77		HaveRefs    []string
78		HaveHashes  []plumbing.Hash
79		Options     AdvancedOptions
80	}
81	
82	func New(opts Options) *Client {
83		return &Client{httpClient: opts.HTTPClient, auth: opts.Auth}
84	}
85	
86	func (c *Client) Probe(ctx context.Context, req ProbeRequest) (ProbeResult, error) {
87		cfg, err := c.buildProbeConfig(ctx, req)
88		if err != nil {
89			return ProbeResult{}, err
90		}
91		result, err := syncer.Probe(ctx, cfg)
92		if err != nil {
93			return ProbeResult{}, fmt.Errorf("probe: %w", err)
94		}
95		return result, nil
96	}
97	
98	func (c *Client) Plan(ctx context.Context, req SyncRequest) (Result, error) {
99		planReq := req
100		planReq.DryRun = true
101		cfg, err := c.buildSyncConfig(ctx, planReq)
102		if err != nil {
103			return Result{}, err
104		}
105		result, err := syncer.Run(ctx, cfg)
106		if err != nil {
107			return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("plan: %w", err)
108		}
109		return result, nil
110	}
111	
112	func (c *Client) Sync(ctx context.Context, req SyncRequest) (Result, error) {
113		cfg, err := c.buildSyncConfig(ctx, req)
114		if err != nil {
115			return Result{}, err
116		}
117		result, err := syncer.Run(ctx, cfg)
118		if err != nil {
119			return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("sync: %w", err)
120		}
121		return result, nil
122	}
123	
124	func (c *Client) Replicate(ctx context.Context, req SyncRequest) (Result, error) {
125		req.Policy.Mode = gitsync.ModeReplicate
126		cfg, err := c.buildSyncConfig(ctx, req)
127		if err != nil {
128			return Result{}, err
129		}
130		result, err := syncer.Run(ctx, cfg)
131		if err != nil {
132			return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("replicate: %w", err)
133		}
134		return result, nil
135	}
136	
137	func (c *Client) Bootstrap(ctx context.Context, req BootstrapRequest) (Result, error) {
138		cfg, err := c.buildBootstrapConfig(ctx, req)
139		if err != nil {
140			return Result{}, err
141		}
142		result, err := syncer.Bootstrap(ctx, cfg)
143		if err != nil {
144			return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("bootstrap: %w", err)
145		}
146		return result, nil
147	}
148	
149	func (c *Client) Fetch(ctx context.Context, req FetchRequest) (FetchResult, error) {
150		cfg, err := c.buildFetchConfig(ctx, req)
151		if err != nil {
152			return FetchResult{}, err
153		}
154		result, err := syncer.Fetch(ctx, cfg, append([]string(nil), req.HaveRefs...), append([]plumbing.Hash(nil), req.HaveHashes...))
155		if err != nil {
156			return FetchResult{}, fmt.Errorf("fetch: %w", err)
157		}
158		return result, nil
159	}
160	
161	func (c *Client) buildProbeConfig(ctx context.Context, req ProbeRequest) (syncer.Config, error) {
162		source, err := c.resolveEndpoint(ctx, req.Source, gitsync.SourceRole)
163		if err != nil {
164			return syncer.Config{}, err
165		}
166		cfg := syncer.Config{
167			Source:        source,
168			HTTPClient:    c.httpClient,
169			IncludeTags:   req.IncludeTags,
170			ShowStats:     req.Options.CollectStats,
171			MeasureMemory: req.Options.MeasureMemory,
172			ProtocolMode:  protocolString(req.Protocol),
173			Verbose:       req.Options.Verbose,
174		}
175		if req.Target != nil {
176			target, err := c.resolveEndpoint(ctx, *req.Target, gitsync.TargetRole)
177			if err != nil {
178				return syncer.Config{}, err
179			}
180			cfg.Target = target
181		}
182		return cfg, nil
183	}
184	
185	func (c *Client) buildSyncConfig(ctx context.Context, req SyncRequest) (syncer.Config, error) {
186		source, err := c.resolveEndpoint(ctx, req.Source, gitsync.SourceRole)
187		if err != nil {
188			return syncer.Config{}, err
189		}
190		target, err := c.resolveEndpoint(ctx, req.Target, gitsync.TargetRole)
191		if err != nil {
192			return syncer.Config{}, err
193		}
194		maxObjects := req.Options.MaterializedMaxObjects
195		if maxObjects == 0 {
196			maxObjects = DefaultMaterializedMaxObjects
197		}
198		return syncer.Config{
199			Source:                 source,
200			Target:                 target,
201			HTTPClient:             c.httpClient,
202			Branches:               append([]string(nil), req.Scope.Branches...),
203			Mappings:               validationMappings(req.Scope.Mappings),
204			IncludeTags:            req.Policy.IncludeTags,
205			DryRun:                 req.DryRun,
206			ShowStats:              req.Options.CollectStats,
207			MeasureMemory:          req.Options.MeasureMemory,
208			Mode:                   operationModeString(req.Policy.Mode),
209			Force:                  req.Policy.Force,
210			Prune:                  req.Policy.Prune,
211			MaxPackBytes:           req.Options.MaxPackBytes,
212			TargetMaxPackBytes:     req.Options.TargetMaxPackBytes,
213			MaterializedMaxObjects: maxObjects,
214			ProtocolMode:           protocolString(req.Policy.Protocol),
215			Verbose:                req.Options.Verbose,
216		}, nil
217	}
218	
219	func (c *Client) buildBootstrapConfig(ctx context.Context, req BootstrapRequest) (syncer.Config, error) {
220		source, err := c.resolveEndpoint(ctx, req.Source, gitsync.SourceRole)
221		if err != nil {
222			return syncer.Config{}, err
223		}
224		target, err := c.resolveEndpoint(ctx, req.Target, gitsync.TargetRole)
225		if err != nil {
226			return syncer.Config{}, err
227		}
228		return syncer.Config{
229			Source:             source,
230			Target:             target,
231			HTTPClient:         c.httpClient,
232			Branches:           append([]string(nil), req.Scope.Branches...),
233			Mappings:           validationMappings(req.Scope.Mappings),
234			IncludeTags:        req.IncludeTags,
235			ShowStats:          req.Options.CollectStats,
236			MeasureMemory:      req.Options.MeasureMemory,
237			MaxPackBytes:       req.Options.MaxPackBytes,
238			TargetMaxPackBytes: req.Options.TargetMaxPackBytes,
239			ProtocolMode:       protocolString(req.Protocol),
240			Verbose:            req.Options.Verbose,
241		}, nil
242	}
243	
244	func (c *Client) buildFetchConfig(ctx context.Context, req FetchRequest) (syncer.Config, error) {
245		source, err := c.resolveEndpoint(ctx, req.Source, gitsync.SourceRole)
246		if err != nil {
247			return syncer.Config{}, err
248		}
249		return syncer.Config{
250			Source:        source,
251			HTTPClient:    c.httpClient,
252			Branches:      append([]string(nil), req.Scope.Branches...),
253			IncludeTags:   req.IncludeTags,
254			ShowStats:     req.Options.CollectStats,
255			MeasureMemory: req.Options.MeasureMemory,
256			ProtocolMode:  protocolString(req.Protocol),
257			Verbose:       req.Options.Verbose,
258		}, nil
259	}
260	
261	func (c *Client) authFor(ctx context.Context, endpoint gitsync.Endpoint, role gitsync.EndpointRole) (gitsync.EndpointAuth, error) {
262		if c.auth == nil {
263			return gitsync.EndpointAuth{}, nil
264		}
265		auth, err := c.auth.AuthFor(ctx, endpoint, role)
266		if err != nil {
267			return gitsync.EndpointAuth{}, fmt.Errorf("resolve auth for %s: %w", role, err)
268		}
269		return auth, nil
270	}
271	
272	func (c *Client) resolveEndpoint(ctx context.Context, endpoint gitsync.Endpoint, role gitsync.EndpointRole) (syncer.Endpoint, error) {
273		auth, err := c.authFor(ctx, endpoint, role)
274		if err != nil {
275			return syncer.Endpoint{}, err
276		}
277		return syncerEndpoint(endpoint, auth), nil
278	}
279	
280	func protocolString(mode gitsync.ProtocolMode) string {
281		if mode == "" {
282			return string(gitsync.ProtocolAuto)
283		}
284		return string(mode)
285	}
286	
287	func operationModeString(mode gitsync.OperationMode) string {
288		if mode == "" {
289			return string(gitsync.ModeSync)
290		}
291		return string(mode)
292	}
293	
294	func syncerEndpoint(endpoint gitsync.Endpoint, auth gitsync.EndpointAuth) syncer.Endpoint {
295		return internalbridge.ToSyncerEndpoint(
296			internalbridge.Endpoint{
297				URL:                    endpoint.URL,
298				FollowInfoRefsRedirect: endpoint.FollowInfoRefsRedirect,
299			},
300			internalbridge.EndpointAuth{
301				Username:      auth.Username,
302				Token:         auth.Token,
303				BearerToken:   auth.BearerToken,
304				SkipTLSVerify: auth.SkipTLSVerify,
305			},
306		)
307	}
308	
309	func validationMappings(mappings []gitsync.RefMapping) []validation.RefMapping {
310		bridgeMappings := make([]internalbridge.RefMapping, 0, len(mappings))
311		for _, mapping := range mappings {
312			bridgeMappings = append(bridgeMappings, internalbridge.RefMapping{
313				Source: mapping.Source,
314				Target: mapping.Target,
315			})
316		}
317		return internalbridge.ToValidationMappings(bridgeMappings)
318	}
319

  "content": "package syncer\n\nimport (\n\t\"fmt\"\n\t\"io\"\n\t\"net/http\"\n\t\"strings\"\n\t\"sync\"\n\t\"sync/atomic\"\n\n\t\"entire.io/entire/git-sync/internal/gitproto\"\n)\n\n// ServiceStats tracks transfer statistics for a single service.\ntype ServiceStats struct {\n\tName          string `json:\"name\"`\n\tRequests      int    `json:\"requests\"`\n\tRequestBytes  int64  `json:\"requestBytes\"`\n\tResponseBytes int64  `json:\"responseBytes\"`\n\tWants         int    `json:\"wants\"`\n\tHaves         int    `json:\"haves\"`\n\tCommands      int    `json:\"commands\"`\n}\n\n// SideBytes reports cumulative bytes transferred at one transport label\n// (\"source\" or \"target\"). Source is dominated by upload-pack response\n// bytes (download), target is dominated by receive-pack request bytes\n// (upload), so this is a useful \"data moved on this side\" number for both.\ntype SideBytes struct {\n\tLabel string `json:\"label\"`\n\tBytes int64  `json:\"bytes\"`\n}\n\n// Stats holds the collected transfer statistics.\ntype Stats struct {\n\tEnabled bool                     `json:\"enabled\"`\n\tItems   map[string]*ServiceStats `json:\"items\"`\n\tSides   []SideBytes              `json:\"sides,omitempty\"`\n}\n\n// sideCounter holds atomic byte counters for one transport label.\n// Updated from the request and response body wrappers without holding\n// the collector mutex, so a progress reader can sample at high\n// frequency without contending with active transfers.\ntype sideCounter struct {\n\tbytes atomic.Int64\n}\n\n// statsCollector is a concurrency-safe stats collector.\ntype statsCollector struct {\n\tenabled bool\n\tmu      sync.Mutex\n\titems   map[string]*ServiceStats\n\tsides   sync.Map // label → *sideCounter\n}\n\nfunc newStats(enabled bool) *statsCollector {\n\treturn &statsCollector{enabled: enabled, items: map[string]*ServiceStats{}}\n}\n\nfunc (s *statsCollector) ensure(name string) *ServiceStats {\n\titem, ok := s.items[name]\n\tif !ok {\n\t\titem = &ServiceStats{Name: name}\n\t\ts.items[name] = item\n\t}\n\treturn item\n}\n\nfunc (s *statsCollector) recordRoundTrip(name string, requestBytes, responseBytes int64) {\n\tif !s.enabled {\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\ts.mu.Lock()\n\tdefer s.mu.Unlock()\n\titem := s.ensure(name)\n\titem.Requests++\n\titem.RequestBytes += requestBytes\n\titem.ResponseBytes += responseBytes\n}\n\n// side returns the per-label counter, creating it lazily on first use.\n// Counters are tracked unconditionally (independent of ShowStats) so the\n// live progress ticker works without forcing --stats.\nfunc (s *statsCollector) side(label string) *sideCounter {\n\tif v, ok := s.sides.Load(label); ok {\n\t\treturn v.(*sideCounter)\n\t}\n\tfresh := &sideCounter{}\n\tactual, _ := s.sides.LoadOrStore(label, fresh)\n\treturn actual.(*sideCounter)\n}\n\n// liveSides returns a snapshot of per-side byte totals for live rendering.\nfunc (s *statsCollector) liveSides() []SideBytes {\n\tvar out []SideBytes\n\ts.sides.Range(func(k, v any) bool {\n\t\tout = append(out, SideBytes{\n\t\t\tLabel: k.(string),\n\t\t\tBytes: v.(*sideCounter).bytes.Load(),\n\t\t})\n\t\treturn true\n\t})\n\treturn out\n}\n\nfunc (s *statsCollector) snapshot() Stats {\n\ts.mu.Lock()\n\tout := Stats{Enabled: s.enabled, Items: make(map[string]*ServiceStats, len(s.items))}\n\tfor key, item := range s.items {\n\t\tcopyItem := *item\n\t\tout.Items[key] = &copyItem\n\t}\n\ts.mu.Unlock()\n\tout.Sides = s.liveSides()\n\treturn out\n}\n\n// countingRoundTripper wraps an HTTP transport to record transfer stats\n// and feed per-side byte counters consumed by the live progress ticker.\ntype countingRoundTripper struct {\n\tbase  http.RoundTripper\n\tlabel string\n\tstats *statsCollector\n}\n\nfunc (rt *countingRoundTripper) RoundTrip(req *http.Request) (*http.Response, error) {\n\tside := rt.stats.side(rt.label)\n\n\t// Wrap the request body so upload bytes (receive-pack POSTs) feed\n\t// the per-side counter as they stream out, not just on round-trip\n\t// completion. Skipped when there is no body (most GETs).\n\tif req.Body != nil {\n\t\treq.Body = &countingReadCloser{ReadCloser: req.Body, side: side}\n\t}\n\n\tres, err := rt.base.RoundTrip(req)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\"round trip: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\n\tserviceName := req.Header.Get(gitproto.StatsPhaseHeader)\n\tif serviceName == \"\" {\n\t\tserviceName = req.URL.Query().Get(\"service\")\n\t\tif serviceName == \"\" {\n\t\t\tserviceName = strings.TrimPrefix(req.URL.Path[strings.LastIndex(req.URL.Path, \"/\")+1:], \"/\")\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tname := strings.TrimSpace(rt.label + \" \" + serviceName)\n\trequestBytes := req.ContentLength\n\tif requestBytes < 0 {\n\t\trequestBytes = 0\n\t}\n\n\tres.Body = &countingReadCloser{\n\t\tReadCloser: res.Body,\n\t\tside:       side,\n\t\tonClose: func(n int64) {\n\t\t\trt.stats.recordRoundTrip(name, requestBytes, n)\n\t\t},\n\t}\n\treturn res, nil\n}\n\ntype countingReadCloser struct {\n\tio.ReadCloser\n\n\tn       int64\n\tside    *sideCounter\n\tonClose func(int64)\n}\n\nfunc (c *countingReadCloser) Read(p []byte) (int, error) {\n\tn, err := c.ReadCloser.Read(p)\n\tif n > 0 {\n\t\tc.n += int64(n)\n\t\tif c.side != nil {\n\t\t\tc.side.bytes.Add(int64(n))\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn n, err //nolint:wrapcheck // Read must preserve io.EOF for io.Reader contract\n}\n\nfunc (c *countingReadCloser) Close() error {\n\terr := c.ReadCloser.Close()\n\tif c.onClose != nil {\n\t\tc.onClose(c.n)\n\t\tc.onClose = nil\n\t}\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"close: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\treturn nil\n}\n"
}

{

  "content": "package syncer\n\nimport (\n\t\"fmt\"\n\t\"io\"\n\t\"os\"\n\t\"sort\"\n\t\"strings\"\n\t\"sync\"\n\t\"time\"\n)\n\n// progressReporter renders live per-side throughput to a writer (typically\n// os.Stderr) by sampling the statsCollector's atomic byte counters on a\n// fixed interval. It is intentionally a one-line in-place renderer so it\n// stays out of the way of the final command output.\ntype progressReporter struct {\n\tout      io.Writer\n\tstats    *statsCollector\n\tinterval time.Duration\n\tstart    time.Time\n\n\tstopOnce sync.Once\n\tstop     chan struct{}\n\tdone     chan struct{}\n\n\tmu      sync.Mutex\n\tlastLen int\n}\n\nfunc newProgressReporter(out io.Writer, stats *statsCollector, interval time.Duration) *progressReporter {\n\tif interval <= 0 {\n\t\tinterval = 200 * time.Millisecond\n\t}\n\treturn &progressReporter{\n\t\tout:      out,\n\t\tstats:    stats,\n\t\tinterval: interval,\n\t\tstart:    time.Now(),\n\t\tstop:     make(chan struct{}),\n\t\tdone:     make(chan struct{}),\n\t}\n}\n\n// run drives the ticker until stop() is called. Safe to call once.\nfunc (p *progressReporter) run() {\n\tdefer close(p.done)\n\tticker := time.NewTicker(p.interval)\n\tdefer ticker.Stop()\n\tfor {\n\t\tselect {\n\t\tcase <-p.stop:\n\t\t\treturn\n\t\tcase <-ticker.C:\n\t\t\tp.render(false)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\n// terminate halts the ticker, draws one final frame so the printed line\n// reflects the closing byte counts, and emits a newline so subsequent\n// command output starts on a fresh row.\nfunc (p *progressReporter) terminate() {\n\tp.stopOnce.Do(func() {\n\t\tclose(p.stop)\n\t\t<-p.done\n\t\tp.render(true)\n\t\tp.mu.Lock()\n\t\tif p.lastLen > 0 {\n\t\t\tfmt.Fprintln(p.out)\n\t\t}\n\t\tp.mu.Unlock()\n\t})\n}\n\nfunc (p *progressReporter) render(final bool) {\n\tsides := p.stats.liveSides()\n\tif len(sides) == 0 && !final {\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tsort.Slice(sides, func(i, j int) bool { return sides[i].Label < sides[j].Label })\n\telapsed := time.Since(p.start)\n\n\tvar b strings.Builder\n\tfor i, side := range sides {\n\t\tif i > 0 {\n\t\t\tb.WriteString(\" · \")\n\t\t}\n\t\tfmt.Fprintf(&b, \"%s: %s @ %s\",\n\t\t\tside.Label, formatBytes(side.Bytes), formatRate(side.Bytes, elapsed))\n\t}\n\tline := b.String()\n\n\tp.mu.Lock()\n\tdefer p.mu.Unlock()\n\tpad := 0\n\tif p.lastLen > len(line) {\n\t\tpad = p.lastLen - len(line)\n\t}\n\tfmt.Fprint(p.out, \"\\r\"+line+strings.Repeat(\" \", pad))\n\tp.lastLen = len(line)\n}\n\n// stderrIsTTY reports whether stderr is attached to a terminal. The\n// progress ticker is suppressed otherwise because '\\r' updates only make\n// sense on a TTY and would otherwise spam log files.\nfunc stderrIsTTY() bool {\n\tfi, err := os.Stderr.Stat()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\treturn (fi.Mode() & os.ModeCharDevice) != 0\n}\n\n// formatBytes renders byte counts in IEC-ish human units (binary base).\nfunc formatBytes(n int64) string {\n\tconst unit = 1024\n\tif n < unit {\n\t\treturn fmt.Sprintf(\"%d B\", n)\n\t}\n\tdiv, exp := int64(unit), 0\n\tfor x := n / unit; x >= unit; x /= unit {\n\t\tdiv *= unit\n\t\texp++\n\t}\n\tvalue := float64(n) / float64(div)\n\tsuffix := []string{\"KB\", \"MB\", \"GB\", \"TB\", \"PB\"}[exp]\n\tif value >= 100 {\n\t\treturn fmt.Sprintf(\"%.0f %s\", value, suffix)\n\t}\n\tif value >= 10 {\n\t\treturn fmt.Sprintf(\"%.1f %s\", value, suffix)\n\t}\n\treturn fmt.Sprintf(\"%.2f %s\", value, suffix)\n}\n\n// formatRate renders a bytes/second average over the supplied duration.\n// Returns \"0 B/s\" until the duration is large enough to be meaningful,\n// avoiding misleadingly large rates from sub-millisecond samples.\nfunc formatRate(bytes int64, dur time.Duration) string {\n\tif dur < 50*time.Millisecond || bytes <= 0 {\n\t\treturn \"0 B/s\"\n\t}\n\trate := float64(bytes) / dur.Seconds()\n\treturn formatBytes(int64(rate)) + \"/s\"\n}\n"
}

787			return Result{}, errors.New("bootstrap does not support dry-run; use plan or sync")
788		}
789	
790		s, err := newSession(ctx, cfg, true)
791		if err != nil {
792			return Result{}, err
793		}
794	
795		desiredRefs, _, err := planner.BuildDesiredRefs(s.sourceRefMap, planConfig(cfg))
796		if err != nil {
797			return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("build desired refs: %w", err)
798		}
799		if len(desiredRefs) == 0 {
800			return Result{}, errors.New("no source refs matched")
801		}
802	
803		_, reason := planner.CanBootstrapRelay(cfg.Force, cfg.Prune, desiredRefs, s.target.refMap)
804		result, err := bootstrapWithInputs(ctx, s, desiredRefs, s.target.refMap, reason)
805		result.Measurement = s.measurementDone()
806		return result, err
807	}
808	
809	// Probe inspects source and optionally target remotes.
810	func Probe(ctx context.Context, cfg Config) (ProbeResult, error) {
811		if cfg.Source.URL == "" {
812			return ProbeResult{}, errors.New("source repository URL is required")
813		}
814	
815		s, err := newSession(ctx, cfg, cfg.Target.URL != "")
816		if err != nil {
817			return ProbeResult{}, err
818		}
819		return s.newProbeResult(), nil
820	}
821	
822	// Fetch exercises source-side fetch negotiation.
823	func Fetch(ctx context.Context, cfg Config, haveRefs []string, haveHashes []plumbing.Hash) (FetchResult, error) {
824		if cfg.Source.URL == "" {
825			return FetchResult{}, errors.New("source repository URL is required")
826		}
827	
828		s, err := newSession(ctx, cfg, false)
829		if err != nil {
830			return FetchResult{}, err
831		}
832	
833		repo, err := git.Init(memory.NewStorage(), nil)
834		if err != nil {
835			return FetchResult{}, fmt.Errorf("init in-memory repository: %w", err)
836		}
837		desiredRefs, err := s.buildDesiredRefs()
838		if err != nil {
839			return FetchResult{}, fmt.Errorf("build desired refs: %w", err)
840		}
841		targetRefMap, err := s.buildHaveRefMap(haveRefs, haveHashes)
842		if err != nil {
843			return FetchResult{}, fmt.Errorf("build have ref map: %w", err)
844		}
845	
846		gpDesired := convert.DesiredRefs(desiredRefs)
847		if err := s.sourceService.FetchToStore(ctx, repo.Storer, s.sourceConn, gpDesired, targetRefMap); err != nil {
848			if !errors.Is(err, git.NoErrAlreadyUpToDate) {
849				return FetchResult{}, fmt.Errorf("fetch to store: %w", err)
850			}
851		}
852	
853		objectCount, err := countObjects(repo.Storer)
854		if err != nil {
855			return FetchResult{}, fmt.Errorf("count fetched objects: %w", err)
856		}
857		return s.newFetchResult(objectCount, desiredRefs, targetRefMap), nil
858	}
859	
860	// --- Bootstrap implementation ---
861	
862	func bootstrapWithInputs(
863		ctx context.Context,
864		s *syncSession,
865		desiredRefs map[plumbing.ReferenceName]planner.DesiredRef,
866		targetRefs map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash,
867		relayReason string,
868	) (Result, error) {
869		bResult, err := bstrap.Execute(ctx, bstrap.Params{
870			SourceConn: s.sourceConn, SourceService: s.sourceService, TargetPusher: s.target.pusher,
871			DesiredRefs: desiredRefs, TargetRefs: targetRefs,
872			SourceHeadTarget: s.sourceService.HeadTarget,
873			MaxPackBytes:     s.cfg.MaxPackBytes, TargetMaxPack: s.cfg.TargetMaxPackBytes,
874			Verbose: s.cfg.Verbose, Logger: s.logger,
875		}, relayReason)
876		if err != nil {
877			return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("bootstrap execute: %w", err)
878		}
879		return Result{
880			Plans: bResult.Plans, Pushed: bResult.Pushed, OperationMode: s.cfg.Mode,
881			Relay: bResult.Relay, RelayMode: bResult.RelayMode, RelayReason: bResult.RelayReason,
882			Batching: bResult.Batching, BatchCount: bResult.BatchCount,
883			PlannedBatchCount: bResult.PlannedBatchCount, TempRefs: bResult.TempRefs,
884			Stats: s.stats.snapshot(), Measurement: s.measurementDone(), Protocol: s.sourceService.Protocol,
885		}, nil
886	}

25	func newSyncLikeCmd(name, short string, dryRun bool, defaultMode gitsync.OperationMode) *cobra.Command {
26		var (
27			mappings    []string
28			jsonOutput  bool
29			sourceAuth  gitsync.EndpointAuth
30			targetAuth  gitsync.EndpointAuth
31			branches    string

39			Short:         short,
40			Args:          cobra.MaximumNArgs(2),
41			SilenceErrors: true,
42			SilenceUsage:  true,
43			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
44				req.Policy.Mode = gitsync.OperationMode(modeValue)
45				req.Policy.Protocol = gitsync.ProtocolMode(protocolVal)
46	
47				if req.Source.URL == "" && len(args) > 0 {
48					req.Source.URL = args[0]
49				}
50				if req.Target.URL == "" && len(args) > 1 {
51					req.Target.URL = args[1]
52				}
53	
54				if branches != "" {
55					req.Scope.Branches = splitCSV(branches)
56				}
57				for _, raw := range mappings {
58					mapping, err := validation.ParseMapping(raw)
59					if err != nil {
60						return fmt.Errorf("parse mapping %q: %w", raw, err)
61					}
62					req.Scope.Mappings = append(req.Scope.Mappings, gitsync.RefMapping{
63						Source: mapping.Source,
64						Target: mapping.Target,
65					})
66				}
67	
68				if req.Source.URL == "" || req.Target.URL == "" {
69					return fmt.Errorf("%s requires source and target repository URLs", name)
70				}
71	
72				client := unstable.New(unstable.Options{
73					Auth: gitsync.StaticAuthProvider{Source: sourceAuth, Target: targetAuth},
74				})
75	
76				var (
77					result unstable.Result
78					err    error
79				)
80				ctx := cmd.Context()
81				switch {
82				case dryRun:
83					result, err = client.Plan(ctx, req)
84				case req.Policy.Mode == gitsync.ModeReplicate:
85					result, err = client.Replicate(ctx, req)
86				default:
87					result, err = client.Sync(ctx, req)
88				}
89				if err != nil {
90					return fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", name, err)
91				}
92				printOutput(jsonOutput, result)
93	
94				if !dryRun && result.Blocked > 0 {
95					return errors.New("one or more branches were skipped because the target was not fast-forwardable")
96				}
97				return nil
98			},
99		}

{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/git-sync/internal/syncer/syncer.go",
  "old_string": "func statsLines(s Stats) []string {\n\tif !s.Enabled {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\tkeys := make([]string, 0, len(s.Items))\n\tfor k := range s.Items {\n\t\tkeys = append(keys, k)\n\t}\n\tsort.Strings(keys)\n\tvar lines []string\n\tfor _, k := range keys {\n\t\titem := s.Items[k]\n\t\tlines = append(lines, fmt.Sprintf(\n\t\t\t\"stats: %s requests=%d request-bytes=%d response-bytes=%d wants=%d haves=%d commands=%d\",\n\t\t\titem.Name, item.Requests, item.RequestBytes, item.ResponseBytes, item.Wants, item.Haves, item.Commands,\n\t\t))\n\t}\n\treturn lines\n}",
  "new_string": "func statsLines(s Stats) []string {\n\tif !s.Enabled {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\tkeys := make([]string, 0, len(s.Items))\n\tfor k := range s.Items {\n\t\tkeys = append(keys, k)\n\t}\n\tsort.Strings(keys)\n\tvar lines []string\n\tfor _, k := range keys {\n\t\titem := s.Items[k]\n\t\tlines = append(lines, fmt.Sprintf(\n\t\t\t\"stats: %s requests=%d request-bytes=%d response-bytes=%d wants=%d haves=%d commands=%d\",\n\t\t\titem.Name, item.Requests, item.RequestBytes, item.ResponseBytes, item.Wants, item.Haves, item.Commands,\n\t\t))\n\t}\n\tif line := throughputLine(s); line != \"\" {\n\t\tlines = append(lines, line)\n\t}\n\treturn lines\n}\n\n// throughputLine renders a one-line per-side throughput summary using\n// the wall-clock window the stats collector observed. Returns \"\" when\n// no side bytes were recorded so the line stays out of the way for\n// metadata-only operations like probe.\nfunc throughputLine(s Stats) string {\n\tif len(s.Sides) == 0 || s.ElapsedNanos <= 0 {\n\t\treturn \"\"\n\t}\n\tsides := make([]SideBytes, 0, len(s.Sides))\n\tfor _, side := range s.Sides {\n\t\tif side.Bytes <= 0 {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tsides = append(sides, side)\n\t}\n\tif len(sides) == 0 {\n\t\treturn \"\"\n\t}\n\tsort.Slice(sides, func(i, j int) bool { return sides[i].Label < sides[j].Label })\n\tdur := time.Duration(s.ElapsedNanos)\n\tparts := make([]string, 0, len(sides))\n\tfor _, side := range sides {\n\t\tparts = append(parts, fmt.Sprintf(\"%s=%s @ %s\",\n\t\t\tside.Label, formatBytes(side.Bytes), formatRate(side.Bytes, dur)))\n\t}\n\treturn \"throughput: \" + strings.Join(parts, \" · \")\n}"
}

  "content": "package syncer\n\nimport (\n\t\"bytes\"\n\t\"strings\"\n\t\"testing\"\n\t\"time\"\n)\n\nfunc TestFormatBytes(t *testing.T) {\n\tt.Parallel()\n\tcases := []struct {\n\t\tin   int64\n\t\twant string\n\t}{\n\t\t{0, \"0 B\"},\n\t\t{42, \"42 B\"},\n\t\t{1023, \"1023 B\"},\n\t\t{1024, \"1.00 KB\"},\n\t\t{1500, \"1.46 KB\"},\n\t\t{int64(15 * 1024), \"15.0 KB\"},\n\t\t{int64(1024 * 1024), \"1.00 MB\"},\n\t\t{int64(150 * 1024 * 1024), \"150 MB\"},\n\t}\n\tfor _, c := range cases {\n\t\tif got := formatBytes(c.in); got != c.want {\n\t\t\tt.Errorf(\"formatBytes(%d) = %q, want %q\", c.in, got, c.want)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc TestFormatRate(t *testing.T) {\n\tt.Parallel()\n\tif got := formatRate(0, time.Second); got != \"0 B/s\" {\n\t\tt.Errorf(\"zero bytes should produce 0 B/s, got %q\", got)\n\t}\n\tif got := formatRate(1<<20, time.Microsecond); got != \"0 B/s\" {\n\t\tt.Errorf(\"sub-50ms windows should produce 0 B/s to avoid bogus rates, got %q\", got)\n\t}\n\tgot := formatRate(1<<20, time.Second)\n\tif got != \"1.00 MB/s\" {\n\t\tt.Errorf(\"1 MiB/s should format as 1.00 MB/s, got %q\", got)\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc TestProgressReporterRendersBothSides(t *testing.T) {\n\tt.Parallel()\n\tstats := newStats(true)\n\tstats.side(\"source\").bytes.Store(2 * 1024 * 1024)\n\tstats.side(\"target\").bytes.Store(1024 * 1024)\n\n\tvar buf bytes.Buffer\n\tp := newProgressReporter(&buf, stats, 0)\n\tp.render(true)\n\n\tout := buf.String()\n\tif !strings.Contains(out, \"source: 2.00 MB\") {\n\t\tt.Errorf(\"output missing source bytes: %q\", out)\n\t}\n\tif !strings.Contains(out, \"target: 1.00 MB\") {\n\t\tt.Errorf(\"output missing target bytes: %q\", out)\n\t}\n\tif !strings.HasPrefix(out, \"\\r\") {\n\t\tt.Errorf(\"output should start with carriage return for in-place updates: %q\", out)\n\t}\n\tif !strings.Contains(out, \"·\") {\n\t\tt.Errorf(\"output should separate sides with a middle dot: %q\", out)\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc TestProgressReporterTerminateEmitsNewline(t *testing.T) {\n\tt.Parallel()\n\tstats := newStats(true)\n\tstats.side(\"source\").bytes.Store(2048)\n\n\tvar buf bytes.Buffer\n\tp := newProgressReporter(&buf, stats, time.Hour) // long interval; we only render manually\n\tgo p.run()\n\tp.terminate()\n\n\tif !strings.HasSuffix(buf.String(), \"\\n\") {\n\t\tt.Errorf(\"terminate should leave the cursor on a fresh line, got %q\", buf.String())\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc TestThroughputLineFormatsBothSides(t *testing.T) {\n\tt.Parallel()\n\tstats := Stats{\n\t\tEnabled:      true,\n\t\tItems:        map[string]*ServiceStats{},\n\t\tElapsedNanos: time.Second.Nanoseconds(),\n\t\tSides: []SideBytes{\n\t\t\t{Label: \"target\", Bytes: 1 << 20},\n\t\t\t{Label: \"source\", Bytes: 4 << 20},\n\t\t},\n\t}\n\tline := throughputLine(stats)\n\tif !strings.HasPrefix(line, \"throughput: \") {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"line should start with 'throughput: ', got %q\", line)\n\t}\n\t// Sides must be ordered alphabetically so output is stable across runs.\n\tsourceIdx := strings.Index(line, \"source=\")\n\ttargetIdx := strings.Index(line, \"target=\")\n\tif sourceIdx < 0 || targetIdx < 0 || sourceIdx > targetIdx {\n\t\tt.Errorf(\"expected source before target in %q\", line)\n\t}\n\tif !strings.Contains(line, \"4.00 MB\") || !strings.Contains(line, \"4.00 MB/s\") {\n\t\tt.Errorf(\"source 4 MiB / 1s should render as 4.00 MB and 4.00 MB/s, got %q\", line)\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc TestThroughputLineEmptyWhenNoBytes(t *testing.T) {\n\tt.Parallel()\n\tstats := Stats{Enabled: true, ElapsedNanos: time.Second.Nanoseconds()}\n\tif got := throughputLine(stats); got != \"\" {\n\t\tt.Errorf(\"expected empty line with no sides, got %q\", got)\n\t}\n}\n"
}

#!/bin/sh
#MISE description="go mod tidy"

fi

TestBootstrap_ThroughputLineAndProgressTicker(t *testing.T) {\n\tsourceRepo, sourceFS := newSourceRepo(t)\n\tmakeCommits(t, sourceRepo, sourceFS, 4)\n\n\ttargetRepo, err := git.Init(memory.NewStorage())\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"init target repo: %v\", err)\n\t}\n\n\tsourceServer := newSmartHTTPRepoServerV2(t, sourceRepo)\n\ttargetServer := newSmartHTTPRepoServer(t, targetRepo)\n\tdefer sourceServer.Close()\n\tdefer targetServer.Close()\n\n\tvar progressBuf bytes.Buffer\n\tcfg := Config{\n\t\tSource:       Endpoint{URL: sourceServer.RepoURL()},\n\t\tTarget:       Endpoint{URL: targetServer.RepoURL()},\n\t\tProtocolMode: protocolModeAuto,\n\t\tShowStats:    true,\n\t\tProgress:     true,\n\t\tprogressOut:  &progressBuf,\n\t}\n\n\tresult, err := Bootstrap(context.Background(), cfg)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"bootstrap failed: %v\", err)\n\t}\n\tif result.Pushed != 1 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"expected one push, got %+v\", result)\n\t}\n\n\t// Per-side counters should record bytes on both sides.\n\tsides := map[string]int64{}\n\tfor _, side := range result.Stats.Sides {\n\t\tsides[side.Label] = side.Bytes\n\t}\n\tif sides[\"source\"] <= 0 {\n\t\tt.Errorf(\"expected non-zero source bytes, got %d\", sides[\"source\"])\n\t}\n\tif sides[\"target\"] <= 0 {\n\t\tt.Errorf(\"expected non-zero target bytes, got %d\", sides[\"target\"])\n\t}\n\tif result.Stats.ElapsedNanos <= 0 {\n\t\tt.Errorf(\"expected non-zero elapsed nanos, got %d\", result.Stats.ElapsedNanos)\n\t}\n\n\t// Human-formatted output should include the new throughput line.\n\tout := strings.Join(result.Lines(), \"\\n\")\n\tif !strings.Contains(out, \"throughput: \") {\n\t\tt.Errorf(\"missing throughput line in output:\\n%s\", out)\n\t}\n\tif !strings.Contains(out, \"source=\") || !strings.Contains(out, \"target=\") {\n\t\tt.Errorf(\"throughput line should mention both sides:\\n%s\", out)\n\t}\n\n\t// Progress writer should have received at least one frame. The bootstrap\n\t// is very fast so we may only get the final terminate() render.\n\tif progressBuf.Len() == 0 {\n\t\t// Allow a brief grace window in case the goroutine had not flushed\n\t\t// yet. terminate() inside finish() blocks on render so this should\n\t\t// be unnecessary, but keep a small fallback for slow CI.\n\t\ttime.Sleep(50 * time.Millisecond)\n\t}\n\tif progressBuf.Len() == 0 {\n\t\tt.Errorf(\"expected progress reporter to write at least one frame\")\n\t}\n\tif !bytes.Contains(progressBuf.Bytes(), []byte(\"source:\")) {\n\t\tt.Errorf(\"progress output should mention source: %q\", progressBuf.String())\n\t}\n\tif !bytes.Contains(progressBuf.Bytes(), []byte(\"target:\")) {\n\t\tt.Errorf(\"progress output should mention target: %q\", progressBuf.String())\n\t}\n}\n"

> AGENT

All green. Here's what shipped:

**End-of-run** (under `--stats`):
```
throughput: source=1.35 KB @ 18.6 KB/s · target=1.29 KB @ 17.7 KB/s
```
"source" = bytes that flowed through the source HTTP transport (dominated by upload-pack response — what we got). "target" = bytes through the target transport (dominated by receive-pack request body — what we pushed). Computed against the stats-collector's own wall clock, so it works without `--measure-memory`.

**Live ticker** (under `--progress`):
```
\rsource: 12.3 MB @ 4.5 MB/s · target: 8.1 MB @ 3.2 MB/s
```
Stderr-only, suppressed automatically when stderr isn't a TTY (so JSON pipes / CI logs stay clean), 200ms refresh, single in-place line that's terminated with a newline so subsequent output isn't mangled.

**Files touched:**
- `internal/syncer/stats.go` — per-side atomic byte counters; wraps both `req.Body` and `resp.Body` so upload bytes count toward the target side
- `internal/syncer/progress.go` (new) — ticker, TTY check, byte/rate formatters
- `internal/syncer/syncer.go` — `Config.Progress`, `syncSession.finish()` deferred from the four entry points, new `throughputLine` in stats output
- `internalbridge/model.go`, `unstable/client.go` — plumb `Sides`/`ElapsedNanos`/`Progress` through public API
- `cmd/git-sync/{sync,replicate,plan,bootstrap,fetch}.go` — `--progress` flag
- Tests: `progress_test.go` + `throughput_test.go` (verifies real bootstrap populates per-side bytes, prints the throughput line, and renders both sides on the live ticker)

Race + lint pass.

> AGENT

Two commits, each self-contained:

1. **`1db3bcf` Track per-side transport bytes for source and target** — pure plumbing. Wraps both request and response bodies in the existing `countingRoundTripper`, adds atomic per-label counters and a wall-clock sample to `Stats` snapshots, plus the matching `internalbridge` fields. Builds, tests, and lints standalone with no callers — counters are just sitting there waiting to be consumed.

2. **`633c57e` Show per-side throughput at end of run and via --progress ticker** — surfacing. Adds the `throughput: source=… · target=…` line under `--stats`, the `--progress` live ticker on stderr (TTY-gated), `Config.Progress` + `syncSession.finish()` plumbing, the `unstable.AdvancedOptions.Progress` field, the four CLI flags, and tests.

Each commit builds and tests cleanly on its own; nothing on `main` is touched.

That's a Go invocation issue, not anything from this branch. `go run cmd/git-sync/main.go` only compiles that single file, so the other files in the package (`root.go`, `syncplan.go`, etc. where `newRootCmd` lives) are missing.

Use the package path instead:

```
go run ./cmd/git-sync sync --progress …
```

Or build once and run:

```
go build -o bin/git-sync ./cmd/git-sync
./bin/git-sync sync --progress …
```

Same problem would have hit you before this branch — nothing about the throughput/progress work changed how main.go is wired.

> AGENT

Two things going on, both around credentials:

1. **Mangled line.** Your target (Cloudflare) is asking for auth — go-git prompts on stderr (you can see the tail of `Username for 'https://…':` poking through), and the progress ticker is also drawing on stderr. They clobber each other. Fix: provide credentials so no prompt fires, e.g.

   ```
   --target-token=$CF_TOKEN
   # or env var:
   GITSYNC_TARGET_TOKEN=$CF_TOKEN go run ./cmd/git-sync sync --progress …
   ```

2. **Only `source:` shown.** Target hasn't completed a single HTTP round trip yet — it's blocked on that credential prompt — so the target counter was never registered. As soon as the first target request fires, you'd see both lines.

If you want, I can land a small follow-up that pre-registers both `source` and `target` at session start, so the line reads `source: … · target: 0 B @ 0 B/s` from the first frame, even before target's first HTTP request. Doesn't fix the prompt collision but it removes the "where's target?" surprise. Want me to?

93			} else {

101		if ep == nil || ep.Hostname() == "" {
102			return ""
103		}
104		var b strings.Builder
105		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "protocol=%s\nhost=%s\n", ep.Scheme, ep.Hostname())
106		if path := strings.TrimPrefix(ep.Path, "/"); path != "" {
107			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "path=%s\n", path)
108		}
109		if ep.User != nil && ep.User.Username() != "" {
110			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "username=%s\n", ep.User.Username())
111		}
112		b.WriteString("\n")
113		return b.String()
114	}
115	
116	func parseCredentialOutput(output []byte) map[string]string {
117		values := map[string]string{}
118		for _, line := range strings.Split(string(output), "\n") {
119			line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
120			if line == "" {
121				continue
122			}
123			k, v, ok := strings.Cut(line, "=")
124			if ok {
125				values[k] = v
126			}
127		}
128		return values
129	}

> AGENT

Found the cause: `internal/auth/auth.go:70` calls `git credential fill` as a subprocess. The child inherits our stderr (`cmd.Output()` only captures stdout), so its `Username for '…':` prompt goes straight to the terminal while our ticker keeps drawing. Two writers, one tty.

The cleanest fix: don't start the ticker until after auth resolution is complete. Auth happens entirely inside `newSession` (in the two `newConn` calls — source first, then target). If we move the ticker start to the very end of `newSession`, any credential prompt fires cleanly to a quiet terminal, and once auth resolves the ticker takes over for the bulk transfer phase. This also accidentally fixes a small leak: if `newSession` errors out, we wouldn't have started a ticker that nobody terminates.

> AGENT

Pushed up as `2e3bd39`. Re-run your earlier command and the credential prompt should fire cleanly before any ticker drawing — once you've answered it (or once the helper caches the creds for next time), the ticker takes over for the actual transfer phase.

Caveat to be aware of: if a credential prompt ever fires *mid-transfer* (essentially never in HTTP git, but theoretically possible), it would still collide. Fixing that case would require intercepting the `git credential fill` subprocess's stderr through a coordinator that pauses the ticker — much more invasive. Happy to tackle that if you ever hit it, but it's not worth the complexity preemptively.

can we do: 

github.com -> 168 MB @ 4.35 MB/s · 168 MB @ 4.35 MB/s -> 8b04592ed74a5cce30d355b07276caf3.artifacts.cloudflare.net

basically take the host names from both sides?

> AGENT

Yes, doable. Layout would be:

```
github.com → 168 MB @ 4.35 MB/s  │  168 MB @ 4.35 MB/s → cloudflare.net
```

Arrows on each side make the data-flow direction self-evident, so the middle separator just needs to mark "two different things". A few options:

| Separator | Look |
|-----------|------|
| `│` (U+2502, light vertical) | `… 4.35 MB/s  │  168 MB @ …` |
| `┃` (U+2503, heavy vertical) | `… 4.35 MB/s  ┃  168 MB @ …` |
| double space | `… 4.35 MB/s    168 MB @ …` |
| `⇢` (dashed arrow) | `… 4.35 MB/s  ⇢  168 MB @ …` |

My pick is **`│`** — clean "this-and-that" divider, doesn't compete with the directional arrows, no risk of being confused for a flow indicator. Alternative I'd accept: just double space and let the arrows carry the visual structure.

One thing to flag: long hostnames (your Cloudflare host is ~57 chars) push the line past 80 cols. If it wraps, `\r` redraws break. I'd suggest just printing the full hostname and adding smart truncation later if it actually bites — most real-world hostnames fit. Alternative is something like `8b04592e…cloudflare.net` from day one.

Which separator do you want, and do you want hostname truncation now or later?

1	package syncer
2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"

14	
15	// ServiceStats tracks transfer statistics for a single service.
16	type ServiceStats struct {
17		Name          string `json:"name"`
18		Requests      int    `json:"requests"`
19		RequestBytes  int64  `json:"requestBytes"`
20		ResponseBytes int64  `json:"responseBytes"`
21		Wants         int    `json:"wants"`
22		Haves         int    `json:"haves"`
23		Commands      int    `json:"commands"`
24	}
25	
26	// SideBytes reports cumulative bytes transferred at one transport label
27	// ("source" or "target"). Source is dominated by upload-pack response
28	// bytes (download), target is dominated by receive-pack request bytes
29	// (upload), so this is a useful "data moved on this side" number for both.
30	type SideBytes struct {
31		Label string `json:"label"`
32		Bytes int64  `json:"bytes"`
33	}
34	
35	// Stats holds the collected transfer statistics.
36	type Stats struct {
37		Enabled      bool                     `json:"enabled"`
38		Items        map[string]*ServiceStats `json:"items"`
39		Sides        []SideBytes              `json:"sides,omitempty"`
40		ElapsedNanos int64                    `json:"elapsedNanos,omitempty"`
41	}
42	
43	// sideCounter holds atomic byte counters for one transport label.
44	// Updated from the request and response body wrappers without holding
45	// the collector mutex, so a progress reader can sample at high
46	// frequency without contending with active transfers.
47	type sideCounter struct {
48		bytes atomic.Int64
49	}
50	
51	// statsCollector is a concurrency-safe stats collector.
52	type statsCollector struct {
53		enabled   bool
54		startedAt time.Time
55		mu        sync.Mutex
56		items     map[string]*ServiceStats
57		sidesMu   sync.RWMutex
58		sides     map[string]*sideCounter
59	}
60	
61	func newStats(enabled bool) *statsCollector {
62		return &statsCollector{
63			enabled:   enabled,
64			startedAt: time.Now(),
65			items:     map[string]*ServiceStats{},
66			sides:     map[string]*sideCounter{},
67		}
68	}
69	
70	func (s *statsCollector) ensure(name string) *ServiceStats {
71		item, ok := s.items[name]
72		if !ok {
73			item = &ServiceStats{Name: name}
74			s.items[name] = item
75		}
76		return item
77	}
78	
79	func (s *statsCollector) recordRoundTrip(name string, requestBytes, responseBytes int64) {
80		if !s.enabled {
81			return
82		}
83		s.mu.Lock()
84		defer s.mu.Unlock()
85		item := s.ensure(name)
86		item.Requests++
87		item.RequestBytes += requestBytes
88		item.ResponseBytes += responseBytes
89	}
90	
91	// side returns the per-label counter, creating it lazily on first use.
92	// Counters are tracked unconditionally (independent of ShowStats) so the
93	// live progress ticker works without forcing --stats.
94	func (s *statsCollector) side(label string) *sideCounter {
95		s.sidesMu.RLock()
96		if sc, ok := s.sides[label]; ok {
97			s.sidesMu.RUnlock()
98			return sc
99		}
100		s.sidesMu.RUnlock()
101	
102		s.sidesMu.Lock()
103		defer s.sidesMu.Unlock()
104		if sc, ok := s.sides[label]; ok {
105			return sc
106		}
107		sc := &sideCounter{}
108		s.sides[label] = sc
109		return sc
110	}
111	
112	// liveSides returns a snapshot of per-side byte totals for live rendering.
113	func (s *statsCollector) liveSides() []SideBytes {
114		s.sidesMu.RLock()
115		defer s.sidesMu.RUnlock()
116		out := make([]SideBytes, 0, len(s.sides))
117		for label, sc := range s.sides {
118			out = append(out, SideBytes{Label: label, Bytes: sc.bytes.Load()})
119		}
120		return out
121	}
122	
123	func (s *statsCollector) snapshot() Stats {
124		s.mu.Lock()
125		out := Stats{Enabled: s.enabled, Items: make(map[string]*ServiceStats, len(s.items))}
126		for key, item := range s.items {
127			copyItem := *item
128			out.Items[key] = &copyItem
129		}
130		s.mu.Unlock()
131		if s.enabled {
132			out.Sides = s.liveSides()
133			out.ElapsedNanos = time.Since(s.startedAt).Nanoseconds()
134		}
135		return out
136	}
137	
138	// countingRoundTripper wraps an HTTP transport to record transfer stats
139	// and feed per-side byte counters consumed by the live progress ticker.
140	type countingRoundTripper struct {
141		base  http.RoundTripper
142		label string
143		stats *statsCollector
144	}
145	
146	func (rt *countingRoundTripper) RoundTrip(req *http.Request) (*http.Response, error) {
147		side := rt.stats.side(rt.label)
148	
149		// Wrap the request body so upload bytes (receive-pack POSTs) feed
150		// the per-side counter as they stream out, not just on round-trip
151		// completion. Skipped when there is no body (most GETs).
152		if req.Body != nil {
153			req.Body = &countingReadCloser{ReadCloser: req.Body, side: side}
154		}
155	
156		res, err := rt.base.RoundTrip(req)
157		if err != nil {
158			return nil, fmt.Errorf("round trip: %w", err)
159		}
160	
161		serviceName := req.Header.Get(gitproto.StatsPhaseHeader)
162		if serviceName == "" {
163			serviceName = req.URL.Query().Get("service")
164			if serviceName == "" {
165				serviceName = strings.TrimPrefix(req.URL.Path[strings.LastIndex(req.URL.Path, "/")+1:], "/")
166			}
167		}
168		name := strings.TrimSpace(rt.label + " " + serviceName)
169		requestBytes := req.ContentLength
170		if requestBytes < 0 {
171			requestBytes = 0
172		}
173	
174		res.Body = &countingReadCloser{
175			ReadCloser: res.Body,
176			side:       side,
177			onClose: func(n int64) {
178				rt.stats.recordRoundTrip(name, requestBytes, n)
179			},
180		}
181		return res, nil
182	}
183	
184	type countingReadCloser struct {
185		io.ReadCloser
186	
187		n       int64
188		side    *sideCounter
189		onClose func(int64)
190	}
191	
192	func (c *countingReadCloser) Read(p []byte) (int, error) {
193		n, err := c.ReadCloser.Read(p)
194		if n > 0 {
195			c.n += int64(n)
196			if c.side != nil {
197				c.side.bytes.Add(int64(n))
198			}
199		}
200		return n, err //nolint:wrapcheck // Read must preserve io.EOF for io.Reader contract
201	}
202	
203	func (c *countingReadCloser) Close() error {
204		err := c.ReadCloser.Close()
205		if c.onClose != nil {
206			c.onClose(c.n)
207			c.onClose = nil
208		}
209		if err != nil {
210			return fmt.Errorf("close: %w", err)
211		}
212		return nil
213	}
214

1	package syncer
2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"io"
6		"os"
7		"sort"
8		"strings"
9		"sync"
10		"time"
11	)
12	
13	// progressReporter renders live per-side throughput to a writer (typically
14	// os.Stderr) by sampling the statsCollector's atomic byte counters on a
15	// fixed interval. It is intentionally a one-line in-place renderer so it
16	// stays out of the way of the final command output.
17	type progressReporter struct {
18		out      io.Writer
19		stats    *statsCollector
20		interval time.Duration
21		start    time.Time
22	
23		stopOnce sync.Once
24		stop     chan struct{}
25		done     chan struct{}
26	
27		mu      sync.Mutex
28		lastLen int
29	}
30	
31	func newProgressReporter(out io.Writer, stats *statsCollector, interval time.Duration) *progressReporter {
32		if interval <= 0 {
33			interval = 200 * time.Millisecond
34		}
35		return &progressReporter{
36			out:      out,
37			stats:    stats,
38			interval: interval,
39			start:    time.Now(),
40			stop:     make(chan struct{}),
41			done:     make(chan struct{}),
42		}
43	}
44	
45	// run drives the ticker until stop() is called. Safe to call once.
46	func (p *progressReporter) run() {
47		defer close(p.done)
48		ticker := time.NewTicker(p.interval)
49		defer ticker.Stop()
50		for {
51			select {
52			case <-p.stop:
53				return
54			case <-ticker.C:
55				p.render(false)
56			}
57		}
58	}
59	
60	// terminate halts the ticker, draws one final frame so the printed line
61	// reflects the closing byte counts, and emits a newline so subsequent
62	// command output starts on a fresh row.
63	func (p *progressReporter) terminate() {
64		p.stopOnce.Do(func() {
65			close(p.stop)
66			<-p.done
67			p.render(true)
68			p.mu.Lock()
69			if p.lastLen > 0 {
70				fmt.Fprintln(p.out)
71			}
72			p.mu.Unlock()
73		})
74	}
75	
76	func (p *progressReporter) render(final bool) {
77		sides := p.stats.liveSides()
78		if len(sides) == 0 && !final {
79			return
80		}
81		sort.Slice(sides, func(i, j int) bool { return sides[i].Label < sides[j].Label })
82		elapsed := time.Since(p.start)
83	
84		var b strings.Builder
85		for i, side := range sides {
86			if i > 0 {
87				b.WriteString(" · ")
88			}
89			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%s: %s @ %s",
90				side.Label, formatBytes(side.Bytes), formatRate(side.Bytes, elapsed))
91		}
92		line := b.String()
93	
94		p.mu.Lock()
95		defer p.mu.Unlock()
96		pad := 0
97		if p.lastLen > len(line) {
98			pad = p.lastLen - len(line)
99		}
100		fmt.Fprint(p.out, "\r"+line+strings.Repeat(" ", pad))
101		p.lastLen = len(line)
102	}
103	
104	// stderrIsTTY reports whether stderr is attached to a terminal. The
105	// progress ticker is suppressed otherwise because '\r' updates only make
106	// sense on a TTY and would otherwise spam log files.
107	func stderrIsTTY() bool {
108		fi, err := os.Stderr.Stat()
109		if err != nil {
110			return false
111		}
112		return (fi.Mode() & os.ModeCharDevice) != 0
113	}
114	
115	// formatBytes renders byte counts in IEC-ish human units (binary base).
116	func formatBytes(n int64) string {
117		const unit = 1024
118		if n < unit {
119			return fmt.Sprintf("%d B", n)
120		}
121		div, exp := int64(unit), 0
122		for x := n / unit; x >= unit; x /= unit {
123			div *= unit
124			exp++
125		}
126		value := float64(n) / float64(div)
127		suffix := []string{"KB", "MB", "GB", "TB", "PB"}[exp]
128		if value >= 100 {
129			return fmt.Sprintf("%.0f %s", value, suffix)
130		}
131		if value >= 10 {
132			return fmt.Sprintf("%.1f %s", value, suffix)
133		}
134		return fmt.Sprintf("%.2f %s", value, suffix)
135	}
136	
137	// formatRate renders a bytes/second average over the supplied duration.
138	// Returns "0 B/s" until the duration is large enough to be meaningful,
139	// avoiding misleadingly large rates from sub-millisecond samples.
140	func formatRate(bytes int64, dur time.Duration) string {
141		if dur < 50*time.Millisecond || bytes <= 0 {
142			return "0 B/s"
143		}
144		rate := float64(bytes) / dur.Seconds()
145		return formatBytes(int64(rate)) + "/s"
146	}

Sides with neither label\n// fall back to \"name: bytes @ rate\".\nfunc formatSide(side SideBytes, dur time.Duration) string {\n\tname := side.Display\n\tif name == \"\" {\n\t\tname = side.Label\n\t}\n\tname = truncateHost(name, maxHostnameWidth)\n\trate := formatBytes(side.Bytes) + \" @ \" + formatRate(side.Bytes, dur)\n\tswitch side.Label {\n\tcase \"source\":\n\t\treturn name + flowArrow + rate\n\tcase \"target\":\n\t\treturn rate + flowArrow + name\n\tdefault:\n\t\treturn name + \": \" + rate\n\t}\n}\n\n// truncateHost shortens long hostnames while keeping the apex domain\n// visible. Returns the original string if it already fits within max,\n// otherwise preserves the trailing two dotted labels (e.g. \"cloudflare.net\")\n// and spends the remaining budget on a prefix from the leading subdomain.\n// Falls back to right-truncation when the apex alone doesn't fit.\nfunc truncateHost(host string, max int) string {\n\tif max <= 0 || len(host) <= max {\n\t\treturn host\n\t}\n\tlabels := strings.Split(host, \".\")\n\tif len(labels) >= 2 {\n\t\tapex := labels[len(labels)-2] + \".\" + labels[len(labels)-1]\n\t\tif len(apex)+2 <= max { // room for at least one prefix char + ellipsis\n\t\t\tprefixBudget := max - 1 - len(apex)\n\t\t\treturn host[:prefixBudget] + \"…\" + apex\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tif max <= 1 {\n\t\treturn \"…\"\n\t}\n\treturn host[:max-1] + \"…\"\n}"

Returns \"\" when\n// no side bytes were recorded so the line stays out of the way for\n// metadata-only operations like probe.\nfunc throughputLine(s Stats) string {\n\tif len(s.Sides) == 0 || s.ElapsedNanos <= 0 {\n\t\treturn \"\"\n\t}\n\tsides := make([]SideBytes, 0, len(s.Sides))\n\tfor _, side := range s.Sides {\n\t\tif side.Bytes <= 0 {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tsides = append(sides, side)\n\t}\n\tif len(sides) == 0 {\n\t\treturn \"\"\n\t}\n\tsort.Slice(sides, func(i, j int) bool { return sides[i].Label < sides[j].Label })\n\tdur := time.Duration(s.ElapsedNanos)\n\tparts := make([]string, 0, len(sides))\n\tfor _, side := range sides {\n\t\tparts = append(parts, fmt.Sprintf(\"%s=%s @ %s\",\n\t\t\tside.Label, formatBytes(side.Bytes), formatRate(side.Bytes, dur)))\n\t}\n\treturn \"throughput: \" + strings.Join(parts, \" · \")\n}",
  "new_string": "// throughputLine renders a one-line per-side throughput summary using\n// the wall-clock window the stats collector observed. Returns \"\" when\n// no side bytes were recorded so the line stays out of the way for\n// metadata-only operations like probe.\nfunc throughputLine(s Stats) string {\n\tif len(s.Sides) == 0 || s.ElapsedNanos <= 0 {\n\t\treturn \"\"\n\t}\n\tsides := make([]SideBytes, 0, len(s.Sides))\n\tfor _, side := range s.Sides {\n\t\tif side.Bytes <= 0 {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tsides = append(sides, side)\n\t}\n\tif len(sides) == 0 {\n\t\treturn \"\"\n\t}\n\tsort.Slice(sides, func(i, j int) bool { return sides[i].Label < sides[j].Label })\n\tdur := time.Duration(s.ElapsedNanos)\n\tparts := make([]string, 0, len(sides))\n\tfor _, side := range sides {\n\t\tparts = append(parts, formatSide(side, dur))\n\t}\n\treturn \"throughput: \" + strings.Join(parts, sideSeparator)\n}"
}

Returns the original string if it already fits within max,\n// otherwise preserves the trailing two dotted labels (e.g. \"cloudflare.net\")\n// and spends the remaining budget on a prefix from the leading subdomain.\n// Falls back to right-truncation when the apex alone doesn't fit.\nfunc truncateHost(host string, max int) string {\n\tif max <= 0 || len(host) <= max {\n\t\treturn host\n\t}\n\tlabels := strings.Split(host, \".\")\n\tif len(labels) >= 2 {\n\t\tapex := labels[len(labels)-2] + \".\" + labels[len(labels)-1]\n\t\tif len(apex)+2 <= max { // room for at least one prefix char + ellipsis\n\t\t\tprefixBudget := max - 1 - len(apex)\n\t\t\treturn host[:prefixBudget] + \"…\" + apex\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tif max <= 1 {\n\t\treturn \"…\"\n\t}\n\treturn host[:max-1] + \"…\"\n}",
  "new_string": "// truncateHost shortens long hostnames while keeping the apex domain\n// visible. Returns the original string if it already fits within width,\n// otherwise preserves the trailing two dotted labels (e.g. \"cloudflare.net\")\n// and spends the remaining budget on a prefix from the leading subdomain.\n// Falls back to right-truncation when the apex alone doesn't fit.\nfunc truncateHost(host string, width int) string {\n\tif width <= 0 || len(host) <= width {\n\t\treturn host\n\t}\n\tlabels := strings.Split(host, \".\")\n\tif len(labels) >= 2 {\n\t\tapex := labels[len(labels)-2] + \".\" + labels[len(labels)-1]\n\t\tif len(apex)+2 <= width { // room for at least one prefix char + ellipsis\n\t\t\tprefixBudget := width - 1 - len(apex)\n\t\t\treturn host[:prefixBudget] + \"…\" + apex\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tif width <= 1 {\n\t\treturn \"…\"\n\t}\n\treturn host[:width-1] + \"…\"\n}"
}
